title: Filibuster Hunt
subject: Texas History
intro: Spanish Texas, around 1800 to 1821. The Spanish government is on the lookout for filibusters. Can you tell who was one and who was not?

questions.q: In Texas history, a filibuster was someone who...
choices: came from another country and tried to take land and power from the government by force
gave very long speeches to delay a vote
was a Spanish soldier guarding the border
was a priest who started missions
questions.explain: In Spanish Texas a filibuster was a foreign adventurer who came to fight the government for land, power and personal gain. (The long-speech meaning in Congress came later.)

questions.q: Which government decided who counted as a filibuster in Texas? (one word)
questions.explain: Texas belonged to Spain until 1821, so it was the Spanish government that called these intruders filibusters.

questions.q: Criterion 1: a filibuster was from a ______ country (not Spanish).
questions.explain: A filibuster was a foreigner. Someone born in Spain or New Spain could rebel, but would not be called a filibuster.

questions.q: Criterion 2: a filibuster came to ______ the government. (one word)
questions.explain: Filibusters came prepared to fight the Spanish government, usually with a small private army.
They wanted to grab land and power in Texas for themselves.

questions.q: Criterion 4: a filibuster wanted personal gain, meaning they wanted to...
questions.explain: Personal gain means wealth: filibusters hoped to get rich.

questions.q: How many of the four criteria must a person meet to be a filibuster?
questions.explain: On the worksheet, only people with a check in every column are filibusters. Missing even one (like not fighting the government) makes it a NO.
Nolan was an American horse trader who led armed men into Texas without permission. He meets all four criteria. Spanish troops killed him in 1801.
Austin was a foreigner who wanted land and wealth, but he asked Spain for permission to bring settlers (1821). He was not prepared to fight the government, so he is a NO.
questions.review: Moses Austin asked permission, did not fight

questions.q: Peter Ellis Bean: filibuster or not?
questions.explain: Bean was an American who rode with Philip Nolan. He was captured by the Spanish when Nolan was killed. Foreigner, fought, wanted land and gain: all four checks.

questions.q: Baron de Bastrop: filibuster or not?
questions.explain: Bastrop was a foreigner who wanted land and money, but he worked with the Spanish government (he helped Austin get permission). No fighting, so NO.
questions.review: Baron de Bastrop helped, did not fight

questions.q: Father Miguel Hidalgo: filibuster or not?
questions.explain: Hidalgo did fight the government (he started Mexico's war for independence in 1810), but he was born in New Spain, not a foreigner. So he is a NO.
questions.review: Father Hidalgo was not a foreigner

questions.explain: Long was an American who led armed expeditions into Texas (starting 1819) and declared Texas independent. All four checks.
Lafitte was a French-born pirate based on Galveston Island who wanted riches and helped filibusters like James Long. Your worksheet counts him as a filibuster.

questions.q: Father Hidalgo fought the Spanish government. What criterion is he MISSING?
questions.explain: Fighting is not enough. Hidalgo was from New Spain (Mexico), so he fails the 'foreigner' test.

questions.q: Moses Austin and Baron de Bastrop are both NO for the same reason. What is it?
choices: They were not prepared to fight the government
questions.explain: Both were foreigners who wanted land and gain, but they worked with Spain instead of fighting it.

questions.q: Who was Philip Nolan's companion that was captured by the Spanish?
questions.explain: Peter Ellis Bean rode with Nolan in 1801 and spent years as a Spanish prisoner.

questions.q: Which filibuster was a pirate on Galveston Island?
questions.explain: Jean Lafitte ran a pirate base at Galveston.

questions.q: Name one person on the worksheet who is a filibuster.
questions.explain: The four filibusters on the sheet: Philip Nolan, Peter Ellis Bean, James Long and Jean Lafitte.
